summary.text: Goodly son of Priam whom Homer names among the nine sons chidden at Hector's ransom and whom Apollodorus counts among the king's children by other women.

story.text: When old Priam prepared to cross the plain to Achilles' hut, he called to nine sons — among them goodly Agathon beside Helenus, Paris, Pammon, Antiphonus, Polites, Deïphobus, Hippothous, and lordly Dius — and wished they had all fallen in Hector's place.
